statement_unchanged: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, and let $\rho$ be smooth on the closure. Prescribe in the prescribed-data lemma either smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$, or smooth outward flux data $g$ with its compatibility condition as in the weak Neumann lemma. Then the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with those data is $C^\infty$ on the closure $\overline\Omega$. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side. Edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded. The existence claims are those of the two weak solvability lemmas; this lemma proves their classical upgrade on the declared domains.
old_strategy:
Local estimate. In an interior patch, or in a flattened smooth boundary/interface patch, write the weak equation in divergence form $\int a_{ij}\partial_ju\,\partial_iv=\int fv+\int G_i\partial_iv$ with the transformed coefficients $	ilde a=|\det D\Phi^{-1}|\,D\Phi\,a\,D\Phi^{\mathsf T}$; positivity of the Jacobian bounds and the bounds on $D\Phi$ preserve uniform ellipticity. Dirichlet data are removed by subtracting the smooth lift $g(y)\eta(t)$ built from a finite subordinate smooth partition and a normal cutoff; smooth Neumann flux is converted to smooth volume data by a collar vector field $G$ with $G\cdot n=g$ and the divergence theorem. For a tangential difference quotient $\delta_h^ku$ with a cutoff $\eta$ supported in a smaller patch, test the weak identity with $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2w)$; change of variables and the product identity give the principal bound $\alpha\|\eta
abla w\|_2^2$ against cutoff terms $C\|u\|_{H^1}[\|\eta
abla w\|_2+\|w\|_2]$, the crucial increment estimates $\|\delta_hu\|_{L^2}\le\|\partial_ku\|_{L^2}$ (from the ACL line identity and Jensen) and $\|\delta_ha\|_\infty\le\|\partial_ka\|_\infty$, and $f,G$ terms; Cauchy-Schwarz and $2AB\le(\alpha/2)A^2+2B^2/\alpha$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]) absorb the gradient terms, giving uniform difference-quotient bounds. The weak second derivatives that are purely tangential (or mixed interior) exist through the bounded functional obtained by passing to the limit of the difference quotients; the Hilbert Riesz representation ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) supplies an $L^2$ representative, with no pointwise derivative or weak subsequence selection. At a boundary or interface the normal second derivative is recovered from $a_{33}\partial_{33}u=f-\operatorname{div}G+\sum_{(i,j)
e(3,3)}a_{ij}\partial_{ij}u+\sum_{ij}(\partial_ia_{ij})\partial_ju$ with $a_{33}\ge\alpha>0$. A finite cover of the compact closure gives global $H^2$ bounds on each declared side. The higher-order induction differentiates the weak equation by tangential multi-indices; the exact coefficient commutator is finite and $H^1$, so the same local estimate raises the regularity by two orders of tangential/mixed derivatives, and the normal-recovery equation raises the remaining normal counts one by one; Dirichlet tangential derivatives keep zero trace and natural tests stay admissible. Classical representative: the Sobolev extension theorem ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]) extends each piecewise $H^m$ class to a compactly supported $H^m(\mathbb R^3)$ function, and the Fourier characterisation of integer-order Sobolev spaces ([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) with Fourier inversion ([[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]]) converts $W^{m,2}$ membership with $m>j+3/2$ into a $C^j$ representative via the absolutely convergent inverse integral. Derivatives agree with the weak ones by testing and Fubini, representatives agree by continuity, and arbitrarily large $m$ gives a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure whose continuous trace is the prescribed one. Existence of the weak solutions is supplied by the prescribed-data and weak-Neumann lemmas ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]).
